headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading errors: kotaemon’s broad egress and file/API-key handling can expose sensitive documents if paired with a content-writing agent that feeds it untrusted outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can produce arbitrary content and has broad network egress; B ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts through a web UI and may treat imported content as knowledge. No shared channel is documented, so the injection path is inferred rather than proven. Because B handles rich content by default, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF A-generated text is imported into B as a document or chat transcript
IF B renders or summarizes that content without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Require manual review before B indexes any A-produced file
Strip instructions from imported content before upload
Use separate workspaces for A and B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to B’s ingestion pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches documents, PDFs, HTML, XLSX, DOCX, chat transcripts, and API keys, and stores data under ./ktem_app_data while calling third-party APIs. A has broad network egress, so if A receives or forwards B’s sensitive inputs, leakage can occur outside the local boundary. The pair therefore presents a default-dangerous exfiltration path.
conditions: IF B indexes documents containing secrets or regulated data
IF A is given access to B outputs or shared files
IF B is configured to use any listed external API backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B’s indexed corpus
Use a local-only backend for B where possible
Separate A and B onto different machines or containers
Rotate any API keys stored in B after testing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation and egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress, and B supports multiple instances plus broad egress and file-backed state in ./ktem_app_data. Even without explicit shared-write evidence, overlapping mutable surfaces and concurrent instances create a plausible conflict over shared files, API usage, or external resources. Uncertainty remains, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A and B are run against the same filesystem path
IF multiple B instances share the same ./ktem_app_data directory
IF both agents target the same external API quota or account
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories to each agent
Run only one B instance per workspace
Use separate API accounts or quotas
Monitor for file-lock or overwrite errors
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can emit content that B may ingest through documents or chat transcripts, and B is a support/RAG system that can turn ingested text into answers. There is no documented verification step between them, so A’s output can cascade into B’s responses. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text as source material
IF B answers users without citation or provenance checks on that source
IF downstream actions are taken from B’s generated answer
mitigations: Require citations for any B answer derived from A
Insert a human review step before B publishes outputs
Mark A-originated content as untrusted in B
Limit B to retrieval-only mode for A content
requires-engineering: add source-verification gates before generation

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles API keys and multiple document classes and may send them to external APIs; A has broad network egress. If regulated or secret-bearing content enters B, the pair can create a compliance breach through uncontrolled outbound processing. No residency or retention controls are documented, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF B processes regulated documents or secrets
IF any listed external API backend is enabled
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to ./ktem_app_data
mitigations: Do not load regulated data into B
Use only approved local models and storage
Review and purge ./ktem_app_data after tests
Confirm API-key handling is disabled in production
requires-engineering: implement residency, retention, and deletion controls
